source_gaps: iPhone: the Apple page does not explain how to turn on Find My, the Find My network or Send Last Location, and gives no steps for playing a sound in the Find My app; it also does not spell out the icloud.com/find Lost Mode steps, so no web-only Lost Mode steps are used. Android: the page says Find Hub is turned on automatically when a Google Account is added, and no setup step is claimed. Samsung: the page covers Samsung Find and SmartThings Find, not Find My Mobile, and names no One UI or model version. Excerpts were taken from WebFetch output, which is processed text; they were not byte-checked against the live HTML.

source_refs.title: How to find your lost iPhone or iPad
source_refs.section: Turning On Lost Mode from Another Device
source_refs.applicability: iPhone or iPad; use the Find My app on another device or a Family Sharing group member's device
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Scroll down to "Lost [Device]," then turn on "Lost Mode."
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Use the Find My app on another device or a Family Sharing group member's device. 1. In the Find My app, go to the Devices tab. 2. Scroll down and select your missing iPhone or iPad. 3. Tap the More button. 4. Scroll down to 'Lost [Device]', then turn on 'Lost Mode'. 5. Follow the onscreen steps if you want to display your contact information on your missing device. 6. Tap 'Activate'.

source_refs.title: How to find your lost iPhone or iPad
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; conditions stated by the page for Lost Mode
source_refs.verified_excerpt: it only appears online and in Lost Mode if the device has been turned on and is connected to Wi-Fi or cellular
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: If the device is off or offline, it only appears online and in Lost Mode if the device has been turned on and is connected to Wi-Fi or cellular. If Stolen Device Protection is on for iPhone, Face ID or Touch ID is required to turn off Lost Mode, even if someone knows your passcode. If Find My wasn't on before the loss, you can't mark the device as lost or remotely erase it.

source_refs.title: Find, secure, or erase a lost Android device
source_refs.applicability: Android; use Find Hub on another Android phone or tablet, or use Find Hub in a browser
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: 1. Open the Find Hub app on another Android phone or tablet, or use Find Hub in a browser. 2. Sign in, then select the lost device. 3. Select 'Play sound'. It rings the device at full volume for 5 minutes, even on silent or vibrate.

source_refs.title: How to locate your lost Samsung Galaxy phone or tablet
source_refs.applicability: Samsung Galaxy phone or tablet; the page names no One UI or model version
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Turn on the switches for "Allow this phone (or tablet) to be found," "Send last location," and "Offline finding."
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Samsung Galaxy: 1. Open Settings, tap Security and privacy, then tap Lost device protection. 2. Turn on the switches for 'Allow this phone (or tablet) to be found', 'Send last location', and 'Offline finding'. 3. Make sure the phone is powered on, connected to a stable network, and signed in to a Samsung account.
